PARKS, RECREATION & COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION

Welcome to the meeting of the Parks, Recreation & Community Services Commission. Meetings are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast
throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs and videotapes of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office by calling
(818) 548-2090. Meetings are also archived on the City website for viewing anytime at www.ci.glendale.ca.us/video_archives.asp.
PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES AND PAGERS WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request.
Assisted listening devices are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for requests regarding sign language
translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
are public records, will be available for review in the Community Services & Parks Administration Office, 613 E. Broadway, Room 120, Glendale, CA 91206. If you have
any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact (818) 548-2782 during regular business hours.

  MEETING AGENDA
  Monday, June 17, 2019, 2:30 p.m.
  Council Chambers, 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor, Glendale, CA 91206
1.  ROLL CALL
  A. Report of Recording Clerk, re: Posting of the Agenda. The Agenda for the June 17, 2019, regular

2.  UPCOMING COUNCIL AGENDA ITEMS
3.  COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
4.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to items not a part of this agenda. Each speaker is allowed five (5) minutes. The
  Commission may question the speaker, but there will be no debate or decision. The Director may refer
  the matter to the proper section for investigation and report.
5.  CONSENT ITEMS (Including Minutes)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the Commission or
  audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such request before a motion is
  proposed.
  A.  Approval of the Minutes of the Commission regular meeting held on May 20, 2019.

6.  REPORTS – INFORMATION ONLY
  A. Maple Park Community Center Annual Report

  C. Senior Services Annual Report
  D. Section Activity Reports
  1.  Park Services
  2.  Recreation & Community Services
7.  ADJOURNMENT
  NEXT MEETING:
  July 15, 2019 – City Council Chambers, 613 E. Broadway
minutes_text:
PARKS, RECREATION & COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION
  MEETING MINUTES
  Monday, June 17, 2019, 2:30 p.m.
  Council Chambers, 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor, Glendale, CA 91206

1.  ROLL CALL

  The meeting was called to order at 2:38 p.m.

  Present: Commissioners Babaian, Kalfayan, Michals, Wolfson, and President Asatryan
  Absent: None

  A.  Report of Recording Clerk, re: Posting of the Agenda. Ms. Moreno Hernandez reported that the
  agenda for the June 17, 2019, regular meeting was posted on the bulletin board outside City Hall
  on or before Friday, June 14, 2019.
2.  UPCOMING COUNCIL AGENDA ITEMS
  Director of Community Services & Parks Onnig Bulanikian read a list of upcoming City Council agenda
  items related to the Community Services & Parks Department (CSP).

  Commissioners asked if we have more sponsors for Cruise Night this year as compared to last year,
  how many sponsors we usually have, and where one can find the sponsorship packages.
3.  COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
  Commissioners asked if staff had an update on a possible dog park location, what funds are available
  for a dog park, if Development Impact Fee (DIF) funds have to be used in the area where the
  development was put it, and if there was an update on non-profit fees.
4.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  None
5.  CONSENT ITEMS (Including Minutes)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the Commission or
  audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such request before a motion is
  proposed.
  A.  Approval of the Minutes of the Commission regular meeting held on May 20, 2019.

  Moved:  Commissioner Michals
  Seconded: Commissioner Kalfayan

  That the minutes of the Commission regular meeting held on May 20, 2019, be approved as
  written.

  A roll call was conducted and Commissioners voted as follows:

  Ayes:  Commissioners Kalfayan, Michals, Wolfson, and President Asatryan
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  None
  Abstain:  Babaian
  1
 6.  REPORTS – INFORMATION ONLY
  A. Maple Park Community Center Annual Report
  Sr. Community Services Supervisor Sevag Garabetian gave a report and PowerPoint presentation
  covering the following topics as they relate to Maple Park Community Center: days/hours of
  operation, indoor and outdoor facilities, shade structure, center-based programs, center-based
  program participation, Therapeutic Recreation programs, Maple Park “Starz” day camp,
  additional/upcoming programs, and fiscal impact.

  Commissioners asked if there has been any damage to the basketball court due to event rentals,
  for the location of the Shane’s Inspiration playground, what the miscellaneous revenue mentioned
  in the report refers to, if we had less equipment rentals, and for the cost of the day camp at Maple
  Park.

  B.  Adult Recreation Center & Senior Programs Annual Report
  Community Services Supervisor Aylin Isayan gave a report and PowerPoint presentation covering
  the following topics as they relate to Adult Recreation Center and Senior Programs: days/hours of
  operation, facility features and amenities, senior programs and events, and fiscal impact.

  Commissioners asked questions about participation for this year as compared to last year, how
  information is disseminated to the public, and the increase in facility rentals.

  C.  Senior Services Annual Report
  Ms. Isayan gave a report and PowerPoint presentation covering the following topics as they relate
  to Senior Services: three (3) components of the Senior Services Program, Supported Services
  Program, Home Delivered Meals Program, Congregate Meals Program, additional funding
  received this year for congregate meals, March for Meals Month, May is Older Americans Month,
  Senior Street Fest, Farmer’s Market coupons, CalFresh, Senior Services funding sources, and
  Senior Services FY 2018-2019 budget.

  President Asatryan asked where the meals are prepared.

  D.  Section Activity Reports
  1.  Park Services
  Mr. Panossian provided a brief overview of work orders completed by Park Services staff in
  the month of May, highlighting projects at Brand Tea House, Lower Scholl Canyon Park, 3200-
  3500 N. Verdugo (median), Pacific Community Pool, and Central Library.

  Commission Michals asked staff to bring back a report to Commission regarding the gender of
  trees in Glendale in response to an e-mail message sent to Mr. Panossian.

  2.  Recreation & Community Services
  Mr. Garabetian gave a report and PowerPoint presentation covering the following topics: City
  wide special events by CSP, Aquatics Program registration, and programs at community
  centers.
7.  ADJOURNMENT
  The meeting was adjourned at 3:21 p.m.
